title: Balanced brackets
description:
Write `bool balanced(std::string_view text)` that checks whether the brackets `()`, `[]` and `{}` in a piece of text are properly matched and nested. Other characters are ignored.

| Text | Balanced? |
|---|---|
| `{[()()]}` | yes |
| `([)]` | no, they overlap |
| `((` | no, never closed |
| `)(` | no, closed before opened |

The classic method uses a stack:

1. On an opening bracket, push it.
2. On a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be its partner; pop it. If the stack is empty or the top does not match, the text is not balanced.
3. At the end the stack must be empty.
hints: Keep the open brackets in a `std::vector<char>` used as a stack. On a closing bracket, first check the stack is not empty, then check `open.back()` is the matching opener, then `pop_back()`.
A small helper that turns a closing bracket into its opening partner (`')'` to `'('`) keeps the comparison short. At the end, the text is balanced only if the stack is empty.
lessonTitle: Vector as a Stack, and Capacity
